messages:
leo: quick sync after the autoscale follow-up — we sketched three surfaces for reserved capacity: micro-reserves per-tenant, a single global prewarm pool, or a layered fast-local + slow-global approach. thoughts?

karen: micro-reserves = best p99 for top customers but kills headroom with many midsize tenants. global pool is cheap but noisy-neighbor risk.

deepak: layered seems pragmatic: tiny local buffer for short bursts, global reservoir for sustained spikes. operator enforces borrowing & reclaiming.

ops-bot: alert: prewarm_pool_util=92% at 2026-02-12T09:12:43Z. consider spill routing.

leo: i like pushing sizing logic into the operator. CP should publish commit (min) + borrow_budget. operator maps borrow_budget -> local headroom and enforces caps.

karen: spill routing when global pool > 90% should steer non-SLA tenants to cheaper model variants rather than hard rejects. better UX and revenue protection.

deepak: operator needs three verbs: admit, borrow, reclaim. plus telemetry: local_util, borrowed_tokens, reclaim_events per-tenant.

leo: here's a tiny prototype config we discussed:
```
reserve_policy:
  local_buffer_tokens: 4000
  local_buffer_ms: 1200
  decay_half_life: 45s
  borrow_charge_per_sec: 0.6
  global_spill_threshold_pct: 90
  max_local_borrow_ewma: 20000
```

karen: billing must tag borrowed tokens separately and show them in console. ops needs alerts if borrow_rate spikes for a tenant.

deepak: edge-case: adversarial microbursts could game decay. fix: cap sustained borrow using EWMA(borrow_rate) + cooldown window.

leo: short decision summary: prototype operator-driven layered reserves. CP surface = commit + borrow_budget. operator owns mapping to local buffers and reclaim policy. fallback = model-variant spill when reservoir low.

ops-bot: note: rollout checklist created: rfc -> sim -> k8s operator PoC -> smoke tests -> canary.

karen: tests: replay mixed-tenant traces (heavy tail), verify billing tags, fallback counts, and reservoir circuit behavior.

deepak: i'll build the simulator and add a "noisy-microburst" scenario to validate caps. assigning to @deepak.

leo: i'll write the follow-up RFC and rollout gates. start with internal-only tenants, then opt-in alpha. watch reservoir_util and borrow_charge metrics.

karen: i'll own dashboards: per-tenant headroom, borrow_e2e_latency, model-spill counts.

leo: short-term decision: layered reserves with operator handoff. next: schedule spikes and owners.
